steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Criminal law deals with offences against the state and society. The state prosecutes, and penalties include imprisonment, fines, and community orders.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Civil law resolves disputes between individuals or organisations. The claimant sues, and remedies include damages (compensation), injunctions, and specific performance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Standard of proof: criminal cases require proof 'beyond reasonable doubt'; civil cases require proof on the 'balance of probabilities' (more likely than not).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: In criminal cases, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) brings the case on behalf of the state. The defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always specify whether you are discussing criminal or civil law Use precise legal vocabulary — 'claimant' not 'plaintiff', 'prosecution' not 'the government' When comparing, consider: who brings the case, standard of proof, type of court, and outcome
